description:
Goal: no clone, collect, placeholder or guard-drop exists only to get a
value past the borrow checker. Where one remains, the ownership shape
around it requires it and the reason is visible in the types.

Why: the workspace already warns on redundant_clone, implicit_clone,
unnecessary_to_owned, iter_cloned_collect and map_clone, so the mechanical
cases are gone. What is left are copies the current signatures REQUIRE: an
accessor that returns an owned value because its callers hold &mut World, a
struct that owns its immutable input beside its mutable working state, a
RefCell emptied through a throwaway value. Each one is a symptom of an
ownership shape; this epic fixes the shapes.

Evidence (develop @ cca160808, non-test sources, ~136k lines):
1476 .clone(), 136 .to_vec(), 39 mem::take/replace, 36 explicit drop(..).
Most clones sampled are key / id / Rc clones into maps and facts and are
not in scope. The sites in scope are named in the child tickets.

Strategy, per ticket:
1. Change the signature (return a borrow, hold a reference, take a slice)
   and let `cargo check` enumerate the dependents.
2. Sort the errors: callers that compile after a trivial edit were pure
   appeasement; callers that fail to borrow interleave a read with a write.
3. Resolve each interleaving caller by, in order of preference:
   a. compute, then commit (finish the reads, then write);
   b. split the borrow (take the field, not the whole; separate input from
      working state);
   c. share by Rc handle, only for data immutable after construction that
      truly outlives the borrow. Last resort: it keeps the clone and makes
      it cheap.
4. If (c) is the only move left for most callers of a ticket, stop and
   report: the knot is the owner itself and needs a design proposal.

Signal: every ticket is a pure refactor. The full gate stays green with no
golden, census or pin movement; any movement is a defect in the change.
Each ticket deletes the copies it makes unnecessary and any comment that
explained them, and reports the clone/to_vec count of the files it touched
before and after.

Order: .1 first -- its error list shows how much of the World accessor
family is pure appeasement versus real interleaving, which sizes .4 and .5.
title: Ownership shapes need no borrow-checker appeasement
